results.title: Frog Detective 3: Corruption at Cowboy County
results.brief_description:
The third and final game in the Frog Detective trilogy finds mystery in Cowboy County, where Frog Detective joins the ‘number-one detective’, Lobster Cop, to solve the case of some stolen hats.
Worm Club combines the series’ usual detective work with the sights and sounds of the Western, as players interview and help a new cast of absurd townsfolk and outlaws. Cowboy County is bigger than the earlier games’ settings, with “vast and rough” terrain to cross. What began as a gag became one of the game’s key features: a scooter system developed by Tom Bowker, turning movement itself into part of the joke.

constellations_primary.name: Soft-boiled detectives
constellations_primary.description: This Constellation follows cosy mysteries where investigation is playful, social and a little strange. In these works, detectives question odd suspects, navigate anxious communities and solve cases where charm, humour and character matter just as much as the truth itself.

results.title_for_label: Frog Detective 2: The Case of the Invisible Wizard
results.description:
Another mystery is afoot in Frog Detective 2: The Case of the Invisible Wizard. In the town of Warlock Woods, a parade welcoming the Invisible Wizard has been mysteriously destroyed. As the ‘second-best detective’, players interview a new cast of low-poly characters and follow clues through gentle, comic conversation.

This second instalment expands the series’ play style with a detective notebook, letting players track interviews and mark residents as suspicious. Composer Dan Golding also develops the game’s playful jazz score, adding different instruments as Frog Detective meets each character. The result is a mystery shaped by humour, rhythm and care.

results.title: [5 Couleurs de France]
results.brief_description:
This film is a TV Color Paris production titled ‘5 Couleurs de France’, which translates as ‘5 Colours of France’. It features a presentation on the 1967 Cannes Film Festival, with a voiceover spoken in English. The 1967 festival was the 20th anniversary of the festival. The film includes snippets of interviews with Claude Lelouche, Sylva Koscina, Robert Bresson, Monica Vitti and Vanessa Redgrave, translated by the narrator.

It also contains footage of film stars and directors at the festival, particularly at the awards ceremony. These include guest of honour Brigitte Bardot, award presenter Virna Lisi and winner of the Palme d’Or (then known as the Grand Prix International du Festival) Michelangelo Antonioni, for his film ‘Blow Up’.

The colour is faded throughout the film.

results.title: The Ferals [Puppets]
results.credit_line:
Designed by Garth Frost

Puppet maker Tina Matthews

Australia, 1993

Courtesy of Emma de Vries

Edie Kurzer, Australia, 2020
results.brief_description: “They discovered fame and fortune and they’re never going back.” Or so proclaimed the catchy hook of The Ferals TV theme song. This kids’ program debuted on ABC TV in 1994 and then, after two successful seasons, it has endured in Australian pop culture. Capitalising on the grunge aesthetic of the time, it followed an unruly bunch of feral animals living in a share house with flatmates played by human actors. The ditzy rabbit Mixy and sassy cat Modigliana were key members of the show, adding to the tradition of children’s programming featuring puppets in starring roles, including Lift Off (1992-95) and Mr Squiggle (1959-99).

constellations_other.name: Australian TV in the 1990s
constellations_other.description: In the 1990s, Australians and Australian culture was changing: so too were the representations of it on television.

results.title: CURIOUS
results.brief_description: Edie Kurzer approached curating CURIOUS much like she does when designing costume for film and TV – by taking inspiration from found objects and combining them to exceed their original function, while also avoiding the obvious.

constellations_primary.name: Clothing, country, character
constellations_primary.description: Edie Kurzer's costume design work on Judy & Punch and Picnic at Hanging Rock is part of a larger trend in Australian films and TV series.

results.description:
When Edie Kurzer is designing costumes for film and TV, she often takes inspiration from found objects. It’s a similar approach to how she has curated these cabinets of curios and memorabilia. Like the details of a costume, when presented together as a collection these objects become more than the sum of their parts. According to Kurzer, “each of the objects have a story to tell, brought together by the common denominator of the moving image”.

Within the cabinets, examples such as the Pez collection or the character figurines celebrate familiar film and TV characters that have escaped the frame and live on as part of our collective memory. Kurzer also acknowledges the behind-the-scenes roles of various creative departments in film and television production through the display of everyday items that are commonly used – a paintbrush, a pair of scissors or a handy wire coat hanger.

In collecting, creating and curating these objects for display, Kurzer adheres to her rule of avoiding the obvious and celebrating the unexpected.

You can see examples of Edie Kurzer’s costume work in The Story of the Moving Image.

results.title: Memoir of a Snail – Grace's hoard
results.brief_description:
Grace goes to live in Canberra with a well-meaning couple whose interests include self-help books, laughing clubs and leaving keys in bowls. To deal with her loneliness, Grace begins hoarding ornamental snails, guinea pigs and romance novels while indulging in Chiko Rolls. It’s to the garden snail Sylvia that Grace tells her story and where Memoir of a Snail gets its name. Over 3000 components were handmade to create Grace’s hoard. The hoarding aspect of the film is inspired by filmmaker Adam Elliot’s experience helping his mother downsize her belongings. He then studied hoarding and found that it often results from trauma and loss, such as Grace experiences in the film.

Memoir of a Snail opens in cinemas October 17, 2024.

constellations_primary.name: Hoarding
constellations_primary.description: In Memoir of a Snail Grace Pudel's collection of guinea pigs and ornamental snails gets out of hand. We all have emotional connection to the objects we collect, but why do we decide to carry these items throughout our lives, and when does a collection become a hoard?

results.title: Gumboots Australia for DOS
results.material_description: Floppy disk videogame. One 3 1/2 inch floppy disk and manual in cardboard box
results.brief_description: Explore Australia and help solve a plethora of mysteries in Gumboots Australia. In this this adventure and educational game, the player is tasked with solving cases as an investigator for the Gumboots Enquiry Agency, a job that will take the player all over the country. The player will get to visit locations as varied as Kakadu to Coober Pedy in their hunt for the next clue. Getting there is its own challenge, as different modes of transportation can cost time and money. Random events along the way aid or hinder the player’s quest to solve the case.
